title: Probabilistic Pager Smoothing + Skeletal On-Call Runbook for Region Evacuation and Load Shedding
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Problem: During partial-region performance degradations we are seeing large bursts of noisy alerts that cause on-call thrash and slow automated failover decisions. Existing alert thresholds are brittle to traffic pattern shifts and our runbooks are long and ambiguous when a rapid region evacuation or targeted load-shedding is required.

Goal: Reduce pager noise via probabilistic smoothing and context-aware suppression while providing a small, deterministic skeletal runbook that automation can drive and human responders can escalate. Ensure automated actions (circuit breaker activation, graceful load-shedding, KV-cache invalidation) are auditable and reversible.

Scope: Adjust alerting rules and debouncing, implement a probabilistic pager-smoothing service that reduces duplicate/low-confidence pages, create a 6-step skeletal runbook for on-call, and wire automation hooks for safe evacuation and circuit-triggered load shedding. Integrations: PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Console dashboards, routing/orchestration service, and existing auto-scale policies.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: (1) Build a lightweight probabilistic scoring service that consumes alert streams and attaches a confidence score based on correlated SLO signals, region health, and anomaly detectors. (2) Use score thresholds and randomized suppression to avoid synchronized suppression across controllers. (3) Implement a fast-path 'operator override' that exposes decision metadata to on-call UIs.

Trade-offs considered: Deterministic suppression avoids surprises but amplifies correlated misses; probabilistic suppression reduces mass-paging but requires careful observability to detect suppressed true positives. We will start conservative (only suppress alerts with confidence < 0.35) and run a 2-week canary on non-prod and a single low-traffic production region.

Engineering tasks: alert rule tuning (Prom/Alertmanager + Console), smoothing service (Go), PL/infra for routing metadata, runbook API endpoints for automation, telemetry instrumenting (trace/span tags), and PagerDuty integration changes.
runbook_snippet:
Skeletal Runbook (6 steps):
1) Acknowledge: Triage owner acknowledges the primary SLO alert and marks region tag.
2) Quick Health Check: Verify region control-plane (APIs, leader heartbeats) and KV latency < X ms. If control-plane down, skip to step 5 (evacuate).
3) Throttle/Protect: Flip safety circuit on heavy-user routes to 10% serve, enable read-only mode where applicable.
4) Apply Targeted Load-Shed: Enable configured shed policy for the affected region (route list).
5) If error-budget burn or control-plane failure: trigger automated evacuation (Evacuation play) via runbook API and notify secondary region owners.
6) Post-action verification and rollback guidance: ensure traffic shifted and health stabilized; if not, escalate to SRE lead.

Each step has a single command/API with an idempotent path and an automatic rollback timeout (default 15 minutes).
alert_rules_changes:
Planned rule adjustments: group related SLO alerts into a single SLO-cluster rule with a moving-window evaluation; add a 'smoothing_score' label produced by the smoothing service; route alerts with smoothing_score < 0.3 to 'suppressed' path with low-urgency; route > 0.7 as P0; introduce grace windows based on request qps percentiles per region.

We will also add dedupe windows and circuit-specific thresholds so that the same underlying failure doesn't create redundant pages (e.g., kernel OOM vs. network partition).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag the smoothing service and suppression path.
2) Canary in dev/staging for 3 days using synthetic generated spikes.
3) Canary to one low-traffic prod region for 7 days, monitor suppressed-true-positive metric and page-to-fix ratios.
4) Expand to non-critical regions over 5 business days.
5) Global rollout conditional on <10% increase in MTTR and >= 60% reduction in duplicate pages.
6) Post-rollout: 30-day watch with daily burn-down emails to owners.

Rollback triggers: suppressed_true_positive_rate > 0.05 or suppressed_alert_unacknowledged > 2x baseline in canary window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic; integration tests across Alertmanager -> smoothing service -> Pager bridge; chaos tests simulating cross-region partitions and traffic bursts; two scheduled simulated incidents during canary with SRE observers. Pre-launch checklist includes PagerDuty run with synthetic page and manual override exercised by on-call.
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Platform, and Product. Agreed on conservative suppression thresholds and the need for full traceability in the Console.
2026-02-28: Prototype smoothing service implemented (score model uses regional SLOs + anomaly score). Initial unit tests passing. Linked design doc and stubbed API endpoints.
2026-03-06: Alert rules branch opened (GH: redwood/reliability#412). Initial Prom/AM config reviewed by monitoring team; suggested adding per-route grace windows.
2026-03-10: Completed skeletal runbook draft; on-call rotation review scheduled. PagerBridge integration prototype posted to internal PR.
2026-03-14: Canary rollout to staging starts. Observability hooks and debug traces visible in Console (trace ids emitted).
review_feedback: From Maya (PM) - 2026-02-25: Keep the auto-evacuation path gated behind a two-step approval for the first production canary. Add explicit customer-impact labels for each affected route.
From Anil (Design) - 2026-03-02: UI for operator override must surface the last 3 suppressed events and the confidence score. Keep the override action audit logged.
From Julio (SRE) - 2026-03-08: Lower initial suppression aggressiveness; suggest start threshold 0.35 and observe for 2 weeks before adjusting.
From Security - 2026-03-10: Ensure runbook API calls are authenticated with short-lived tokens and operations logged to audit service.
final_notes: Next steps: finish canary, execute two operator-simulated incidents during the staging canary window, and collect feedback from two on-call rotations. Prepare a short runbook training session for SRE and Platform rotation owners. After 30-day watch, evaluate whether to extend probabilistic logic to non-SLO alerts.
